title: Confirmatory R1 (false-done gate) on the OSWorld LibreOffice subset, OSWorld's own task configs, controller, evaluator and Claude runner on the Myco Linux fleet, graded by OSWorld's own evaluate path
ruling: Lead rulings 2026-11-27: 13:55Z (#700 comment 7220110528, approved 14:00Z: each benchmark's own task configs, action server and evaluators, unmodified; Claude via the benchmark's standard computer-use runner; Myco adds only the completion gate before DONE); 14:05Z (#741 comment 7220313158: RETARGET to the Myco Linux fleet with a DesktopEnv provider adapter used by every arm, parity against OSWorld's reference before any live run, measurements; supersedes the environment part of 13:55Z); 14:37Z (#741 comment 7220987945: the accessibility tree and pyautogui/python-xlib in the fleet image and provider; re-measure, also actively driven; keep the parity harness, do not run it); 15:21Z (#741 comment 7221935698: UTM approved as the parity reference hypervisor, a stated deviation; never a Broadcom/VMware account).

rulings.summary: Harness: the benchmark's own task configs, controller, evaluators and standard Claude runner; Myco adds only the DONE gate (approved 14:00Z).
Retarget: OSWorld LibreOffice subset on the Myco Linux fleet; a provider adapter used by every arm; parity before any live run; WAA phase 2; no paid box or second VM.
Scope: a11y tree (GTK3 VCL plugin, AT-SPI bus before Calc) and pyautogui/python-xlib in the image and provider with tests; extended measure.sh incl. actively driven; parity harness kept but not run.

UTM (QEMU/HVF) approved for the parity reference run, recorded as a stated deviation from OSWorld's VMware reference; guest image, controller and evaluator unchanged; nothing downloads until the ~40 GB disk question is answered.

harness.name: OSWorld
harness.controller: desktop_env/controllers/python.py#PythonController, talking to OSWorld's own desktop_env/server at the pin, run unmodified inside each fleet desktop

provider.name: myco-fleet
provider.imageDigest: PENDING: the sha256 digest of the fleet image as built by the coordinator; every arm runs this one digest
provider.registration: src/benchmark/upstream/fleet/desktop_env_providers.patch adds the name myco-fleet to desktop_env/providers/__init__.py and to DesktopEnv's clean-start provider set, nothing else; desktop_env.evaluate is untouched
provider.reset: A fresh container per task (no snapshots), as OSWorld's own docker provider resets

harness.pinnedFiles: SHA-256 of every harness file in src/benchmark/upstream/pins.ts OSWORLD_HARNESS.files (patched files: OSWORLD_HARNESS.patchedFiles) and every fleet file in MYCO_FLEET.files; a run on any other bytes, another provider or an unpinned image is ungradable

agentRunner.modifications: None except the DONE gate hook (src/gate-hooks/osworld/myco_done_gate.py), wired by the documented patch surface in docs/benchmark/upstream/gate-hook.md. Arms no-gate and self-check run the same wrapper with the gate bypassed by configuration.

model: PENDING: the exact Claude model id passed as --model; it must be one the pinned runner accepts (mm_agents/anthropic/utils.py)

actionLayer.path: AnthropicAgent.predict -> lib_run_single.run_single_example -> DesktopEnv.step -> PythonController.execute_python_command / execute_action; observations from DesktopEnv._get_obs
actionLayer.assertion: Identical across arms: the same runner, environment, provider (myco-fleet, one image digest), controller, action space, observation type and budget in all three arms. The gate hook takes only the agent, never the environment or controller, and returns the agent's actions unchanged except a refused DONE, which becomes upstream's own WAIT special action (a no-op in the guest). Tested with fakes in test/benchmark/osworld-gate-hook.test.ts.

gateInterception.where: Between AnthropicAgent.predict and DesktopEnv.step, in lib_run_single.run_single_example's loop: DoneGate.predict wraps the agent and inspects its returned actions for upstream's DONE special action (AnthropicAgent emits DONE when Claude ends a turn without a tool call).
gateInterception.how: On DONE, the hook calls myco_gate_check with taskId, runId and claim only. verified with accepted:true passes DONE through unchanged (the runner ends the episode and calls env.evaluate()). Anything else (refuted, uncertain, malformed, unreachable) replaces DONE with WAIT and gives the agent one user message with the verdict and reason codes only; the agent continues within the same step budget.
gateInterception.agentFacingReply: verdict and reason codes only; never the gate's prose or corrections

arms.description: (a) OSWorld's standard Claude runner, no gate: DONE is accepted as upstream accepts it.
(b) The same runner; DONE is intercepted and accepted only on a verified gate verdict.
(c) Strongest honest self-check baseline: the same runner with prompt-level self-verification before DONE (AnthropicAgent's own system_prompt_suffix), no gate.
arms.promptSuffix: Before you finish, verify your own work. Take a screenshot and check every requirement of the task against what is actually on screen and in the saved file: the exact values, the cells, text or slides the task names, nothing else changed, and the document saved under the requested name, location and format. If anything is wrong or unsaved, fix it and check again. Only stop calling tools when you have checked that the task is fully complete.

budget: PENDING: one budget for all three arms: --max_steps (the runner default is 15; the Claude example in OSWorld's SETUP_GUIDELINE.md uses 50), --max_tokens, --thinking, --max_trajectory_length, and a wall-clock cap
subsetRule: Every task id listed in OSWorld's evaluation_examples/test_all.json at the pinned commit under libreoffice_calc, libreoffice_writer and libreoffice_impress, run in OSWorld's own DesktopEnv on the myco-fleet provider. No Myco placement filter; the apps a task needs and the getters its evaluator uses are not exclusions. No task is added or dropped for difficulty, outcome or evaluator type.

grader.description: The upstream evaluation path unmodified: DesktopEnv.evaluate() runs the task's postconfig through its setup controller, its own getters through the in-VM controller and its own metrics, with the FAIL-action rule; lib_run_single writes the score to result.txt. Myco only reads that file (src/benchmark/upstream/r1-grade.ts) and refuses any run whose harness bytes differ from the pin.

parity.rule: Parity must pass before any live run. A pre-declared sample of OSWorld LibreOffice tasks, each with a scripted known-good and known-bad action sequence, is scored by upstream DesktopEnv.evaluate() on the Myco fleet and on the reference environment and recorded per task (src/benchmark/upstream/parity.ts assessParity). Parity passes only when every sample task gives the same status on both; any mismatch is a stated gap, reported with the exact host requirement.

reference.guestImage: Ubuntu-arm.zip from huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_osworld (the image OSWorld's VMware manager selects on a Mac, desktop_env/providers/vmware/manager.py:27,35 @ 0ad41bee): 12,287,865,453 bytes; 25,215,685,544 bytes unzipped in 27 files (a split vmdk); its Ubuntu.vmx sets memsize 4096, numvcpus 2
reference.deviation: STATED DEVIATION from OSWorld's VMware reference (lead ruling 15:21Z): only the hypervisor differs. The guest image, its in-guest controller and OSWorld's evaluator are unchanged; UTM boots the same split vmdk. Never VMware Fusion or any Broadcom/VMware account.
reference.hostRequirement: docs/benchmark/upstream/host-requirements.md, 'The parity reference run': at least about 40 GB free on the volume holding the VM, 4 GiB guest RAM, one heavy VM at a time under the VM lock, $0 and no accounts

parity.status: Not run. The reference run waits for Tiffany's OK and the ~40 GB disk question (14:37Z, 15:21Z); nothing is downloaded.

gateOracle: PENDING: the gate's oracle family for OSWorld LibreOffice end states (the main build item)
gateOracleConstraint: The gate's oracle must be independent of the upstream evaluator: no import of desktop_env.evaluators (metrics or getters), no shared code, no reading of evaluator output (result.txt, scores) or of gold files (cloud_file expected assets). Enforced for src/gate and src/gate-hooks by test/benchmark/independence.test.ts.
falseDone: The agent says DONE; OSWorld's own evaluate path scores the end state below the pass threshold or the run is ungradable. In the gate arm, the gate either caught it (did not accept) or did not (accepted: a false accept).
primaryOutcome: False accepts in the gate-before-done arm: trials where the gate accepted DONE and OSWorld's evaluate path did not pass. Bar: 0, with the Wilson 95% upper bound on the false-accept rate reported. An accepted claim the evaluator cannot grade counts against the bar.
secondaryOutcomes: Each arm's false-done rate and success rate under the same upstream grader
Paired gate-before-done vs no-gate and gate-before-done vs self-check tables with exact sign tests on discordant pairs (underpowered below 6 discordant pairs, as R2)
Cost per verified task per arm (R7 rule: totals over all trials over the verified count)
evidenceRules: Only LIVE rows graded by OSWorld's evaluate path at the pin count. MOCK, scripted or simulated rows, and rows from the MOCK metric runner (upstream-metric-mock/1), are refused.
Every result line states task set, n, model, baseline, grader, and live or mock.
A frozen pre-registration is never edited after its data exists.
phase2: WAA office subset (64 tasks @ eb220c4dcf64) via WAA's own Windows 11 image, in-VM server, evaluators and runner: deferred, not dropped.
leadRulingPending: asset-license: OSWorld's own setup downloads the seed and gold files from the xlangai/ubuntu_osworld_file_cache dataset, whose terms are unclear (README §1); no live run until ruled
model: the exact Claude model id
budget: the shared step, token, thinking and wall-clock budget
n: 117 (every task in the three LibreOffice domains, one trial each) is this draft's proposal, not ratified; whether to add repetitions is open
pass-threshold: an upstream score of exactly 1.0 is a pass (most OSWorld metrics are 0/1; a few return fractions)
gate-oracle: which gate oracle family the gate-before-done arm uses on these end states, independent of the upstream evaluator
parity-reference-run: the parity reference run (OSWorld's Ubuntu-arm.zip in UTM) waits for Tiffany's OK and the ~40 GB disk question (15:21Z); parity must pass before any live run

self-check-form: arm (c) is a prompt suffix through AnthropicAgent's system_prompt_suffix; the structural alternative (intercept the first DONE as the gate does, WAIT plus a fixed oracle-free re-check message, same budget) needs a lead ruling (#741 round-1 verdict N3)
model-access: the pinned runner calls the Anthropic API (or Bedrock/Vertex) with a key; M2's rule is $0 API on the Claude Ultra plan, so how the runner reaches the model needs a ruling
